boundaries.registration: engine_cleanup_add_last(Some(engine_list_cleanup)) in engine_list_add, only when the list first becomes non-empty
boundaries.body: loop { if !lock() { return; } let head = ENGINE_LIST_HEAD.load(Ordering::Acquire); if head.is_null() { unlock(); return; } let removed = unsafe { engine_list_remove(head) }; unlock(); if removed == 0 { return; } }
precondition_set: the calling thread does not already hold the engine lock
boundaries.disposition: REPAIR RECORDED: the TOCTOU at this site is eliminated at 0d39697ae, not documented. The head is loaded under the engine write lock that also performs the removal, so no head value crosses an unlock. This receipt claims no SAFETY_DISCHARGED verdict for the site; the site-scoped discharge remains r13-coordinate-rebind's transcription of boundary-sweep-B56, and an independent BOUNDARY review of this repair is NOT_RUN.
boundaries.contract: engine_list_cleanup takes no caller arguments. The engine lock must be initialised and must not already be held by the calling thread; the lock is taken before the head read and released after the removal. The list can only become non-empty through ENGINE_add, whose engine came from ENGINE_new/ENGINE_by_id, both of which initialise the lock. With a NULL lock, lock() answers false and the cleanup returns with the list intact: a documented no-op/leak, not undefined behaviour. The concurrent-remover exclusion that the older record asked the caller to establish is now structural: every unlink of a list member and every release of a member's structural reference requires the same engine write lock, so for the whole critical section the observed head is the list head and holds a live structural reference.
established: src/engine/eng_list.rs:158-180 at 0d39697ae: lock(); load(Acquire); null check; engine_list_remove(head); unlock() — the load and the removal are inside one lock/unlock pair.
